tb21_profile.skill: Enumerate every JavaScript injection vector in HTML (script tags, on* handlers, javascript:/data: URIs, srcdoc, svg, style, meta refresh) and strip exactly those while leaving all other markup byte-faithful
tb21_profile.domain: Python HTML parsing and sanitization (BeautifulSoup/html5lib/lxml/bleach), web XSS security
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec: a small argv[1] CLI that rewrites a file in place, judged adversarially on both a malicious corpus (must strip) and a benign corpus (must not alter)

searches: tools.py words rebench HTML script tag attribute parse sanitize XSS escape element

TMax-15K.reason: Deliverable is a sanitizer.py CLI that HTML-encodes <script>/javascript: without stripping safe characters, graded against thousands of payloads - the same task.
Adversarial filter that must reject 100% of HTML-tag and javascript: payloads while preserving 100% of the clean corpus; identical precision/recall tension.
Defeats a WAF that strips <script> and javascript: using <svg onload=...>; teaches exactly the vectors a naive JS filter misses.
Builds a pipeline around the bluemonday HTML sanitizer to strip HTML from text while keeping content - same library category and preserve-the-rest goal.
Patch an XSS hole by escaping user fields with Python's html module before they reach an HTML report; escape-not-delete reasoning.
A stdin filter that URL-decodes then strips the literal <script>; fixing it exposes the classic decode-then-filter bypass a correct sanitizer must avoid.
Parses HTML with beautifulsoup4 and maps h1/p/a to Markdown; requires walking a real HTML tree rather than regexing tags.
Adversarial bundle filter rejecting <script>, <iframe and comment-embedded directives; practice enumerating injection vectors, but reject-whole-file not surgical removal.
Fix improper handling of user input that is interpolated into a generated HTML report (XSS plus command injection) in an existing tool.
Sanitize payloads and self-report whether <script> survived; same sanitize-and-verify loop but only one vector is considered.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Reads an HTML CV, checks which required sections it contains, and proves every one survives the transform - content-preservation verification like filter.py's benign corpus.
Converts HTML and then generates an automated report confirming key content sections survived; transform-without-losing-content discipline.
Must honour meta tags found in the HTML source during conversion and validate the result; forces actually parsing the head, not pattern matching.
Parses an HTML reference document from a shell script and extracts matching records; HTML-as-input text processing.
Same HTML colour table, but must emit one formatted line per match with values pulled out of the markup; extraction accuracy over a real HTML file.
Write a filter script that removes only the nodes carrying a forbidden key and writes the rest unchanged; the same remove-a-subset-preserve-the-rest contract on JSON.
Rewrites one specific construct in every JavaScript file in place, leaving the rest of each file untouched; in-place surgical source rewriting.
Same in-place JS import rewrite with the target read from config; adds discovery but no new parsing skill.
Downloads a page with its resources and archives them; touches HTML resource references but the work is mostly tooling and packaging.
Turns a script into a proper sys.argv CLI with error handling; matches only the argv[1]-script shape of filter.py.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Parse a real news-article HTML file and emit only the body text with no markup; requires a parser that survives messy real-world HTML.
page-loader must find every local resource reference in the downloaded HTML and rewrite those attributes while leaving the document otherwise intact.
Runs a WCAG checker over every HTML file in a tree, which means reasoning per element and attribute about what the markup declares.
Scrapy spider that selects titles out of page markup and follows pagination links; selector-based HTML tree navigation.
Scrape a profile listing page into structured JSON; extracting specific elements from HTML without mangling the rest.
Scrapes a dealer-locator page across several queries; parsing server-rendered HTML forms and result tables.
Escapes exactly the characters outside a safe range into \uXXXX and passes everything else through; identical transform-only-the-unsafe-substrings contract.
Rewrites one construct across five JavaScript files in place; matches the edit-files-in-place shape, not the HTML reasoning.
jq filter that drops only the objects carrying a given key and keeps the rest; remove-a-subset semantics on a different tree format.
Generates a browsable static HTML site from a repo with an off-the-shelf tool; HTML is only the output format.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: bleach must escape unknown HTML-like tags to <...> instead of emitting them; that decision is the core of any JS-stripping filter.
HTML entities inside anchors must survive bleach untouched - exactly the 'output identical except the removals' requirement, on the same library.
urlsplit mishandles non-special schemes; scheme parsing is precisely what decides whether an href is javascript: and must be dropped.
Breaks bleach's active-formatting-elements bookkeeping on nested links; fixing it means understanding the HTML tree-building a sanitizer relies on.
Wrong HTML escaping output, explicitly framed as an XSS-prevention regression; the escape table must be exactly right.
Renderer fails to escape special characters into HTML output, opening XSS; same escape-on-output correctness the filter needs.
Vendored URL parser mishandles delimiters at position 0, so netloc and path come out wrong - bad URL parsing means bad href filtering.
bleach's nofollow callback crashes while rewriting link attributes; attribute-rewriting plumbing in the sanitizer itself.
Attribute-value selector matching over a BeautifulSoup tree is broken; selecting elements by attribute is how a sanitizer finds on* handlers.
escape() does not escape the ampersand first, producing broken entities; the classic ordering bug in hand-written HTML escapers.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Parser crashes on unclosed tags inside code spans mixed with raw <div> blocks; raw-HTML-block handling is exactly the edge case filter.py must survive.
A tag present in the input is silently lost on markup round-trip; the same fidelity failure the benign-HTML half of this task punishes.
xmltodict returns a string for one child tag and a list for several, corrupting the parse; a markup-tree pitfall that also bites HTML walkers.
Duplicate text generated when rendering an HTML document with RTL runs; debugging an HTML parse-to-render pipeline for output fidelity.
Write/read XML round trip loses float typing; same write-then-reparse-must-match invariant, different markup and domain.
An expected element is never emitted on export; markup serialization completeness, only loosely related to HTML sanitization.
Flex layout bug driven from a concrete HTML/CSS document; same stack (HTML plus CSS in Python) but layout, not sanitization.
Markup-to-HTML toolchain breaks on reference resolution; document-transform debugging with only incidental HTML content.
Cookie parsing collapses on a bare cookie; web-security-adjacent header parsing, reproduced with an inline <script> response.
Errback results discarded in the scraping framework; shares only the lxml/parsel HTML-scraping ecosystem, no markup reasoning.

final_top10.reason: Its deliverable is a CLI sanitizer that HTML-encodes <script>/javascript: without touching safe characters, graded on thousands of payloads.
Filter must reject every HTML-tag and javascript: payload while preserving the clean corpus perfectly - the same two-sided grading.
Bug in the canonical Python HTML sanitizer about escaping unknown tags instead of emitting them; that call is filter.py's core decision.
Entities inside anchors must round-trip through bleach unchanged, the same preserve-everything-else constraint in the same library.
Bypasses a filter that strips only <script> and javascript: with <svg onload=...>; teaches the vectors an incomplete JS filter leaves open.
URL scheme parsing for non-special schemes is wrong; deciding whether an href is javascript: depends on exactly this.
Builds a pipeline on the bluemonday HTML sanitizer to strip markup from text while keeping the content intact.
HTML escaping emits the wrong entity, framed explicitly as an XSS regression; the escape table must be exactly right.
A stdin filter that URL-decodes then strips the literal <script>; repairing it surfaces the decode-then-filter bypass a real sanitizer must close.
Parses HTML with beautifulsoup4 and maps elements to Markdown, forcing real tree traversal rather than tag regexes.

notes: SWE-Smith is unusually strong here because it contains the mozilla/bleach repo (7 tasks) plus markupsafe, mistune, dominate and soupsieve - I found these with my own searches, not from the shortlist, whose top entries were driven by the word 'key'. The shortlist for TMax was also mostly noise (forensics/crypto tasks matching on 'filter'/'HTML report'); the two best TMax candidates (task_004544_3403e2f6, task_005319_0d19e265) were only reachable by searching for sanitizer/XSS wording. RTS has no HTML-sanitization task at all - a regex for sanitize/xss/<script>/BeautifulSoup over 37k RTS instructions returned one irrelevant hit - so its ten are HTML-to-PDF content-preservation and in-place-rewrite tasks with honestly low scores. SWE-Rebench likewise has nothing: no bleach, no sanitizer, only markup round-trip and HTML-rendering bugs. I deliberately included attacker-side XSS tasks (task_007206_2ea22c7f) because knowing the evasion vectors is what separates a complete filter from a <script>-only one.
